metadata.title: Relational-Algebraic Pregeometry: Finite Kernels, Open Continuum Emergence, and Formal Verification
metadata.description:
Relational-Algebraic Pregeometry: Finite Kernels, Open Continuum Emergence, and Formal Verification presents RAP v4.0: a falsification-first re-architecture of the historical UIDT programme. The continuous scalar S(x) is retained only in a non-imported historical appendix. The active candidate is a finite relational-algebraic kernel at evidence class [D], with an open continuum-emergence programme, a commit-scoped Lean 4 formalization record, and a separate verification and parameter ledger.

Relational-Algebraic Pregeometry v4.0 | Falsification-First Kernel Programme | Finite Kernel → Open Continuum | CC BY 4.0

Version scope: this metadata draft follows the corrected RAP v4.0 working text. The DOI below identifies the supplied v4.0 base record; it does not assert registration or independent verification of a later correction.

Abstract

The active foundational layer contains no classical scalar field, background spacetime, metric, or smooth-manifold primitive. The finite candidate is represented through the formal separation BlockPartition → FiniteAlgebraSignature → SpectralTriple. This is a research architecture, not a completed construction of physical spacetime or matter. The scalar-gradient obstruction, the origin of GSM, the Born rule, Lorentzian signature, and the H0/S8 questions remain explicit boundaries.

Part I develops the kernel candidate, the G1–G4 obstruction analysis, and a corrected admissibility lattice. Under the declared H1/H2 predicates, an elementary interval theorem classifies admissible sorted partitions; the special case N = 6 uniquely yields [3,2,1]. Neither the mathematics nor its reported Lean formalization derives the filters physically. Division-algebra and matrix-attractor approaches remain bounded comparison programmes. Part II records the unresolved passage to apparent continuity and is capped at [E] wherever it becomes interpretive. Part III separates benchmark comparison and retained parameter definitions from active ontology.

The historical scalar/EFT axioms, Lagrangian, and background-metric ansatz remain visibly marked museum material. Their preservation supplies provenance, not premises for the active kernel. RAP v4.0 claims a falsifiable programme, conditional results, and localized obstructions—not a completed derivation of spacetime, the Standard Model, or its empirical parameters.

Programme Scope

This is a foundations-and-architecture record. No Clay-level Yang–Mills mass-gap solution, Standard-Model-origin theorem, Born-rule derivation, Lorentzian-signature mechanism, or resolution of cosmological tensions is claimed. Successful compilation, numerical proximity, and governance approval do not establish a physical interpretation.

Evidence Grammar and Strata

Six classes are used: [A] for mathematical closure under stated assumptions, exact identities, or explicitly typed deterministic, documentary, and policy statements; [A−] for calibrated internal closure, not derivation; [B] for benchmark-related physics at its stated source and uncertainty status; [C] for the cosmology cap; [D] for a falsifiable research programme; and [E] for interpretive, speculative, withdrawn, or museum content. A policy, an input definition, and a proof are not interchangeable merely because the ledger uses the same tag.

A residual below 10⁻¹⁴ at 80-digit working precision is an observed computation, not by itself an exact certificate or rigorous error bound. Exact arithmetic, certified enclosures, or an explicit error analysis is needed for the stronger claim. Stratum I contains empirical inputs; Stratum II contains established theory under its assumptions; Stratum III contains RAP-specific hypotheses and interpretation. No Stratum-III mapping becomes empirical evidence by analogy.

Key Relations

Kernel chain: BlockPartition → FiniteAlgebraSignature → SpectralTriple [D] as a physical programme.

Specific failed scalar-gradient route: A = dS ⇒ F = d²S = 0 [A].

Open gauge-origin bridge: kernel → 𝒜 → GSM [D]. For the spectral-triple route pursued here, candidate checks include non-Abelian matrix structure, rank resources, real structure, and chirality. Passing these checks is not sufficient for a physical derivation.

Exact interval theorem under H1/H2: [m+k−1,…,m], with m ≥ 1, k ≥ 2 and N = km + k(k−1)/2. Here H1 bounds adjacent differences by one; H2 requires at least two pairwise-distinct positive parts. Their physical justification remains open.

Gamma discipline: γ = 16.339 [A−], calibrated and not RG-derived. The separately reported γMC = 16.374 ± 1.005 is not merged with it. The difference is dimensionless: 0.035; dividing by the quoted spread gives 7/201 ≈ 0.03483. This is not a certified significance level without the spread convention, calibration uncertainty, and covariance.

Retained coupling identity: adopting κ = 1/2 and 5κ² = 3λS gives λS = 5/12 exactly [A]. Rational arithmetic gives zero residual. This does not prove an RG fixed point, external agreement, or the dimensionful value v = 47.7 MeV. The latter remains a separate historical ledger input; its retained [A] notation denotes definition/transcription, not a physically exact VEV or zero experimental uncertainty.

Automorphism convention: complex-linear *-automorphisms of MN(ℂ) form PU(N); ordinary complex algebra automorphisms form PGLN(ℂ). The *-condition cannot be silently omitted.

Core Contributions

  • Ontological re-architecture: a finite [D] kernel replaces the historical scalar primitive without importing a continuum or Standard-Model conclusion.
  • Localized obstructions: G1–G4 and the corrected lattice separate algebraic requirements from inserted physical assumptions.
  • Conditional mathematics: the interval theorem and special N = 6 result are separated from the missing derivation of H1/H2.
  • Commit-scoped formalization: declaration-level proof status, remaining proof debt, build reachability, and unresolved target-shape auditing are not conflated.
  • Non-ontological ledger: retained calibrations and benchmark comparisons do not become kernel predictions.
  • Audit apparatus: limitations L1–L15, eight advisory gates, tensions T1–T9, and a 28-item gap atlas record what remains open.
  • Historical retention: the scalar/EFT record remains visible, citable, and non-imported.

The Eight Falsification Gates — Advisory, Non-Approving

  • F1 — Target separation: enforce the conservative no-access policy and audit calibration/model-selection provenance. Accessibility alone is not a theorem of dependence.
  • F2 — Precision and exactness: use exact arithmetic where possible; otherwise a separate 80-digit context. Setting shared mp.dps inside a function is not isolation; mp.workdps restores settings but is not a separate context.
  • F3 — Benchmark accounting: require source provenance, an uncertainty budget, and covariance treatment. The existence of a rule does not certify that every benchmark has passed.
  • F4 — L12 separation: no Δ-to-glueball identification without operator matching.
  • F5 — Gauge-origin honesty: keep GSM origin open and selection claims conditional.
  • F6 — Observer boundary: phenomenological reports do not validate the ontology.
  • F7 — Born-rule status: the rule is borrowed from established quantum theory, not derived here.
  • F8 — Governance boundary: no machine verdict or checked theorem alone authorizes a merge, freeze, or physics upgrade.

These are standing audit policies, retained under [A] in the manuscript's grammar—not eight empirical findings. Passing them is necessary hygiene, not sufficient warrant.

Final Forbidden Claims

  • No derivation of GSM, spacetime, Lorentzian signature, or the Born rule from the kernel.
  • No solution of consciousness or validation by psychedelic, near-death, or mystical experience.
  • No ET threshold for life, death, ego, or AGI without a physical scale bridge.
  • No Δ/glueball identity without operator matching; no lattice-compatible number presented as a Clay-level construction.
  • No cosmological tension resolution or validation beyond the stated [C] calibration role.
  • No unconditional physical selection inferred from the N = 6 theorem or from its formal proof.
  • No VEV derivation or RG fixed point inferred from the retained dimensionless coupling identity.
  • No exact proof inferred solely from a rounded residual, and no proof of historical target fitting inferred from primality.
  • No use of museum or quarantined FSS/P2 material as active physical evidence.

These prohibitions are scope and governance constraints, not independent discoveries about nature.

Evidence and Foundations

The external literature supports comparison, scope control, and benchmark selection. It does not replace the RAP evidence hierarchy, derive the finite kernel, or upgrade a RAP-specific mapping. UIDT denotes the historical lineage rather than the active ontology.

The guide foregrounds finite real spectral triples and algebraic multiplicity for Part I; emergent-time and observer comparisons for Part II; and pure-gauge benchmarks or cosmological calibration for Part III. Evidence tags describe RAP’s use of a source, not a universal grade assigned to that source’s research.

Entries marked † are supplementary sources from the supplied comparison list, not entries in the corrected manuscript bibliography used for this update. Their inclusion here does not silently amend the PDF or certify their scientific claims. The remaining entries correspond to intended manuscript references, with metadata corrected where identified; this guide is not a new full-text audit of the complete bibliography.

Finite Algebras, Real Spectral Triples, and the Spectral Standard Model

  • Paschke and Sitarz (1998) — Discrete spectral triples and their symmetries. Real-structure and representation-theoretic foundations.
  • Ćaćić (2011) — Moduli spaces of Dirac operators for finite spectral triples. Multiplicity matrices and moduli; classification does not fix RAP input data.
  • Chamseddine and Connes (1997) — The Spectral Action Principle. Spectral-action comparison under its stated geometric assumptions.
  • Chamseddine, Connes, and Marcolli (2007) — Gravity and the standard model with neutrino mixing. Almost-commutative Standard-Model construction; not derivation from the RAP kernel.
  • Chamseddine, Connes, and van Suijlekom (2013) — Beyond the Spectral Standard Model: Emergence of Pati–Salam Unification. Comparison of admissible algebraic routes and their assumptions.
  • Chamseddine and van Suijlekom (2019) — A survey of spectral models of gravity coupled to matter. Survey context; retain both authors and do not invent a theorem citation.
  • Iochum, Schücker, and Stephan (2004) — On a classification of irreducible almost commutative geometries. Classification constraints; not a derivation of the general H1/H2 filters.
